notebook: Feed 3300 mol/s, 16 comps C2(184.6K)..C9(424K). All-pure value $3615M/yr; normalizer $439M/yr (n-pentane). Blends are contiguous in boiling order and lose only ~12-15% vs pure: C3mix(propyl+propane), C4mix(iC4+nC4), C5mix(iC5+nC5), C6par(22DMB+2MP+3MP+nC6), C6naph(MCP+cyC6). Natural train: C2 / C3mix / C4mix / C5mix / C6par / C6naph / C7 / C8 / C9 = 9 groups, 8 cuts. Ethane tiny (34 mol/s, $4M) - cheap easy split, may just make a small C2 top. Cost scaling observed: 15st/r1=$95M, 30st/r2=$146M(total), 40st/r3=$195M; root30=$120M, sub30 on 647mol/s=$16M => cost ~ throughput*stages*reflux. 5 stages fails converge; keep >=15. Hardest split 3MP/nC6 (~336-342K) vs MCP(345K)=3K. Plan: rebuild root, then sequential train of ~8 columns producing contiguous blend cuts; tune reflux/stages to reach 95%. Calibrate cost vs throughput first with this probe.
